The test image shows tomato plants in a field with black plastic mulch. The center plants are severely wilted/collapsed — complete whole-plant drooping — while neighboring plants remain healthy. No visible leaf spots, mold, or fruiting bodies at this scale. This pattern of sudden, localized whole-plant collapse is characteristic of a vascular wilt or soilborne pathogen.

Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows the classic bacterial streaming test for Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) — a stem cross-section in water with white bacterial ooze streaming from vascular tissue, confirming this is the vascular wilt class.

The test image shows:
- Sudden, complete whole-plant collapse of center tomato plants
- Adjacent plants fully healthy (localized, not spreading uniformly)
- Field on black plastic mulch in warm, dry conditions
- No visible mold, leaf spots, or stem lesions

This pattern — rapid wilt of entire plants in isolation — is the hallmark field presentation of Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum), which invades and blocks vascular tissue, causing plants to suddenly collapse.
